implementation_notes: kotlinx.coroutines supplies the channel as SharedFlow: a MutableSharedFlow is the private publisher side (emit for suspending sends, tryEmit for non-suspending ones) and asSharedFlow exposes the read-only view so only the owner publishes, while each collector is an independent subscriber. A shared flow is hot, thread-safe, never completes, and its replay cache plus extraBufferCapacity with an overflow strategy encode the delivery policy explicitly. Java callers can be served through java.util.concurrent.Flow if the project must stay coroutine-free.
pitfalls: Collecting a shared flow never completes, so a subscription lives until its coroutine scope is cancelled (or a terminal operator like take is applied).
tryEmit returns false when the buffer is full under the default SUSPEND strategy: check the result or configure DROP_OLDEST/DROP_LATEST deliberately.
With no replay and no subscribers the emitted value is dropped outright; a naive test race can look like a broken publisher.
